programmes.d: In addition to Carlin, Johnny is joined by Flip Wilson, Susan St. James and Ann Margaret.
Carlin talks about going on vacation after months on the road, and Johnny chats with Gene Hackman, Mclean Stevenson and Gloria De Haven.
Carlin does stand up and gets sentimental about his 13th wedding anniversary. Also appearing are Jack Knight, Marvin Hamlisch and Jackie Cooper.
It's a double-dose of comedy legends as George Carlin and Richard Pryor stop by The Tonight Show to discuss breakfast food, the LA County Jail and everything in between.
No holiday is safe: Halloween, Thanksgiving and Easter all get the Carlin stand up treatment in this episode also featuring Keshia Knight Pulliam.
National Spelling Bee Champion Jon Pennington joins Johnny on the couch and George Carlin does a routine about losing things.
The wonders of Zest soap are a topic of conversation for Carlin and Johnny in this episode that also features Barney Odum and Flat Nose the tree-climbing dog.
Carlin and Carson talk about writing a sequel to the Bible, Susan Sullivan dreams of Johnny and Sheryl Lee Ralph doesn't need a husband.
George Carlin doesn't feel great, but he looks great! Mark Harmon is a big Carlin fan, and Johnny feels left out.
Watch a Tea Time movie with Carol Wayne. Plus Doris Day has a bad neck, Rodney Dangerfield performs and Burt Mustin discusses his first visit to Hollywood in 1925.
Paul Reiser talks about getting a sensitive body part stuck in an exercise machine. In case you need more reasons to watch, Margaret Whitton and Teresa Ganzel also appear.
The Mighty Carson Art Players do an "Hourly News" sketch. Appearing on the couch are Buddy Hackett, Dave Thomas and Teresa Ganzel.
Jack Benny talks about his NBC special and Rick Little impersonates celebrities. Plus, Johnny takes on gas rationing in his monologue.
Jack Benny doesn't enjoy Paris and Joe Namath doesn't understand politics. Elke Sommer also appears.
You'll love Lucy when she gets a surprise visitor to The Tonight Show. You might also love Dom Deluise and Charlton Heston in this star-studded episode.
George Burns takes on Groucho Marx and young people and Rodney Dangerfield continues to get no respect. Plus, Johnny talks with Michael Constantine and Shana Alexander.
Jackie Gleason opens up about why he quit The Honeymooners after only three years. Plus, Jim Stafford stops by and Johnny jokes about Tommy Lasorda.
Join Johnny as he celebrates Milton Berle's 75th year in show business! Also, Carol Siskind does stand-up and Don Yesso details being discovered on an airplane.
American comedian and beloved star in France, Jerry Lewis jokes about scoring the French Legion of Honor Award and his recent heart surgery.
Merry Christmas, Mr. Hope! Bob says he's spending the holiday with his grandkids in Reno. Producer Gil Cates spills the beans on celebrity game show, What's My Line?
The inimitable Bob Hope offers his 2 cents on the Reagan - Carter debate, sleeping in the Lincoln bedroom, and grades Presidents Johnson and Kennedy on their sense of humor.
Bob Hope talks about growing up poor, his brief boxing career, Christmas in Palm Springs and what it means when a man wears a red tie.
It's Christmas tonight, with Bob Hope in cheery holiday spirit chatting about shopping trips and hitting the golf course over the holidays.
Dom Deluise on earthquakes, Bruno Vailati on sharks and Sally Kellerman on the Queen of England highlight this episode. Plus, Ronnie Schell does stand-up.
Learn how to raise rabbits on a Brooklyn fire escape with Buddy Hackett and how to light a fire with Brady Watt. Also appearing are McLean Stevenson and John Kidner.
